title: 含线路阻抗的对称 Y–Y 电路：归结为一相
statement: 对称三相电源（正序，V̇_A = 220∠0° V）经三根端线向对称星形负载供电，没有中线。每根端线的阻抗 Z_l = 1 + j1 Ω，每相负载 Z = 5 + j7 Ω。
求线电流 I_A、负载相电压 V_{A'N'} 和负载端线电压 V_{A'B'}（均为有效值）。

questions.ask: 负载相电压有效值 V_{A'N'} = ?
questions.explain: V_{A'N'} = I_A·|Z| = 22 × √(5² + 7²) = 22 × 8.602 ≈ 189.25 V，比电源相电压低，因为线路阻抗上有压降。

questions.ask: 负载端线电压有效值 V_{A'B'} = ?
没有中线，为什么还可以把 N' 与 N 短接、只算 A 相？
choices: 对称时由结点电压法 V̇_{N'N} = (V̇_A + V̇_B + V̇_C)/3 = 0，N' 与 N 等电位，短接不改变任何电流
因为 N' 点实际上接地了
这是一种近似，只有线路阻抗很小时才成立
因为 A 相电流最大，只需要算 A 相
choiceExplain: N' 没有接地，图中也没有这根线；能否短接只取决于 N' 与 N 之间的电压，与接不接地无关。
这不是近似：只要电源和每相阻抗（包括端线阻抗）都对称，V̇_{N'N} 就严格为零，与线路阻抗大小无关。
对称时三相电流大小相等，没有哪一相最大；选 A 相只是习惯，算出后另外两相依次差 120° 写出。
questions.explain: 以 N 为参考点列 N' 的结点方程，三相电压之和为零，所以 V̇_{N'N} = 0。等电位的两点之间接一根导线不会有电流，于是可以“加上”一根理想中线，三相各自独立，只算一相即可。

hints: 先说明 V̇_{N'N} = 0，然后画出 A 相的单相电路：V̇_A、Z_l、Z 串联。
I_A = V_A / |Z_l + Z|，负载相电压 = I_A·|Z|。
负载端的三个相电压仍然对称，所以线电压是相电压的 √3 倍。
solution: **1. 中性点电压。** 以 N 为参考，对 N' 列结点方程：V̇_{N'N}·3/(Z_l + Z) = (V̇_A + V̇_B + V̇_C)/(Z_l + Z) = 0，所以 V̇_{N'N} = 0。

en.title: Balanced Y–Y with line impedance: the per-phase equivalent
statement: A balanced three-phase source (positive sequence, V̇_A = 220∠0° V) feeds a balanced wye load through three lines, with no neutral wire. Each line has impedance Z_l = 1 + j1 Ω and each load phase is Z = 5 + j7 Ω.
Find the line current I_A, the load phase voltage V_{A'N'} and the line voltage at the load V_{A'B'} (all rms).

questions.explain: Per-phase circuit: V̇_A across Z_l + Z = 6 + j8 = 10∠53.13° Ω, so I_A = 220/10 = 22 A.
V_{A'N'} = I_A·|Z| = 22 × √(5² + 7²) = 22 × 8.602 ≈ 189.25 V, lower than the source phase voltage because of the drop across the line.

questions.ask: rms line voltage at the load V_{A'B'} = ?
questions.explain: The load voltages are still balanced, so V_{A'B'} = √3 × V_{A'N'} = √3 × 189.25 ≈ 327.79 V.

questions.ask: There is no neutral wire. Why may we still join N' to N and solve phase A alone?
choices: In a balanced circuit nodal analysis gives V̇_{N'N} = (V̇_A + V̇_B + V̇_C)/3 = 0, so N' and N are at the same potential and joining them changes no current
It is an approximation that only holds when the line impedance is small
Because phase A has the largest current, only phase A needs solving
choiceExplain: N' is not earthed and no such wire is drawn; whether the short is allowed depends only on the voltage between N' and N, not on any ground.
It is not an approximation: as long as the source and every phase impedance (line impedance included) are balanced, V̇_{N'N} is exactly zero, whatever the size of the line impedance.
In a balanced circuit the three currents have equal magnitudes, so none is largest; phase A is picked only by convention, and the other two follow by shifting 120°.
questions.explain: With N as reference, the node equation at N' contains the sum of the three phase voltages, which is zero, so V̇_{N'N} = 0. A wire between two points at equal potential carries no current, so an ideal neutral can be “added”; the three phases become independent and one of them suffices.

hints: First show that V̇_{N'N} = 0, then draw the phase-A circuit: V̇_A, Z_l and Z in series.
I_A = V_A / |Z_l + Z|, and the load phase voltage is I_A·|Z|.
The three load phase voltages are still balanced, so the line voltage is √3 times the phase voltage.
solution: **1. Neutral-point voltage.** With N as reference, the node equation at N' reads V̇_{N'N}·3/(Z_l + Z) = (V̇_A + V̇_B + V̇_C)/(Z_l + Z) = 0, so V̇_{N'N} = 0.
Check: each line loses I²·1 = 484 W, each load phase absorbs I²·5 = 2420 W, and each source phase delivers V·I·cos53.13° = 220 × 22 × 0.6 = 2904 W = 484 + 2420.
